answer: Model this with CRMsci, not bare CRMbase. The leg-clipping is an instance of S2 Sample Taking (a subclass of S1 Matter Removal, whose scope note gives 'taking a tissue sample from a body' as a paradigm example and whose superclasses also include E80 Part Removal as a sibling branch). S2 carries O1 diminished -> the moth (as S10 Material Substantial, the material-substantial aspect every E18 Physical Thing has) and O5 removed -> a new S13 Sample. S1's own scope note is explicit on the identity question: 'The removed matter may acquire a persistent identity of different nature beyond the act of its removal, such as becoming a physical object in the narrower sense. Such cases should be modelled by using multiple instantiation with adequate concepts of creating the respective items.' That settles the case's disjunction: the extract is a new object (an S13 Sample, later an S11 Amount of Matter once dissolved), not the moth's own identity continued under a new number. The moth keeps its original identity and catalogue number, now missing a leg (diminished, not destroyed). Whether the extract still counts as coming from the paratype is unaffected by this identity choice: that provenance is carried by the explicit O3 sampled from / O5 removed link recorded on the S2 Sample Taking event, not by the extract sharing the moth's identity. Dissolving the leg into a liquid extract does not, by itself, break the sample's identity either: per S11 Amount of Matter's scope note and the S11 mailing-list debate (t1080), a sample's identity criterion is 'preservation of a relevant composition from the initial state of definition onwards' (here, the DNA), not stability of physical form -- Martin Doerr and Franco Niccolucci both argue samples survive splitting, re-bottling and (implicitly) dissolution as long as the tracked composition persists. So the frozen extract can be the same S13 Sample instance as the removed leg tissue, just re-identified with a new P1/P48 identifier for freezer tracking, still linked back to the paratype moth via the S2 event.

rejected_alternatives.option: Record the extract as the pinned moth's own identity continued under a new number (no new object)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: S1 Matter Removal's scope note explicitly instructs the opposite for matter that acquires a persistent identity of a different nature after removal: model it via multiple instantiation with concepts for creating the item, i.e. as a new object -- not as the source object's continued identity. E18 Physical Thing also requires 'a relatively stable form'; a pinned moth and a liquid freezer extract do not share that identity criterion.

rejected_alternatives.option: E80 Part Removal alone, without the CRMsci sampling classes
rejected_alternatives.why_not: concept S1 shows E80 is a sibling subclass of S1 Matter Removal alongside S2 Sample Taking; E80's own scope note and required properties (P112 diminished, P113 removed) only cover the moth-side diminishment, not the sample's own persistent identity or its link back to the source, which S2's O3 sampled from / O5 removed are declared specifically for.

S3's scope note says it applies when 'the sample is typically not identified and preserved beyond the context of this activity' and explicitly says O5 removed -> S13 Sample need not be instantiated in that case. Here the extract IS preserved under its own catalogue number in a freezer, so S2 Sample Taking (with O5 removed instantiated) is the right fit, not S3.

notes: The `connect` tool did not surface O1/O3 (domain S1/S2, range S10) for either connect E20 S13, connect E20 E80, connect S2 E20, or connect S1 E20, even though concept S10's own dossier declares 'Superclass of: S11, S14, E18' -- i.e. CRMsci's own declaration makes E18 (and hence E20) a subclass of S10. concept E18 itself, however, only lists 'Subclass of: E72' with no mention of S10. So the cross-model subsumption is asserted from the S10 side but not surfaced by connect or visible from the E18 side -- a real gap in what the tools put in front of you, worth flagging rather than papering over. I relied on the textual scope notes (S1, S2, S10, S11, S13) rather than the connect tool for the E20/S10 relationship. Also could not resolve 'S24 Sub-Sampling' by ID via `concept` (returned 'No such concept'), so I did not use it even though it appears as a range in S13's and S2's property lists.
